design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (maturity_due_and_payable_cases, env_0064). Frozen 2026-10-09 14:05:00 EDT (Friday).

1. DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}. Root maturity_ext_further_extension_sizing (6 factors); prerequisite maturity_ext_further_extension_ask (6 factors, customer's own write). One value_input edge (floor max(1-1,1)=1).

2. WHY A GOOD TEST. Dolores Nakamura, a Summit borrower who moved into assisted living and is selling, asks only that her October 13 deadline be moved so the November 20 closing can happen. The case is already in its extension period and her pending request (received 2026-10-07) rests on a listing agreement from March. The agent must read that a further extension waits on a request with current evidence (dated no more than 30 days before receipt), find that the pending one fails it, ask her for newer paperwork, hand her the re-filing with the figure the ask rule computes from her payoff file, occupancy finding, appraisal age, filing lead and reserve, and then size the further extension from the re-filed commitment with Cedarline-side factors (equity, prior grant, reserve charges at closing, occupant, reappraisal). Both numbers need records from five products.

3. SCOPE. Claims maturity_ext_further_extension_ask (supplement_extension_request_11bdc0c2, user) and maturity_ext_further_extension_sizing (grant_further_extension_50c8b1d2, agent); disjoint from task 0's four policies/tools. Together the two tasks cover all six extended policies. (The tool name submit_further_extension_request_d5cdfbad drafted in plan v2 was never written; the re-filing design replaced it.)

4. ROUTE-AROUNDS. The requested days of the customer's re-filing have no stored field: they form part of the new request's reference number and are printed on the receipt with the deadline they would reach (docstring says exactly that). The earlier request is left on file unchanged (a user tool does not decide requests); the grant rests on the most recently received request awaiting a decision, as the rules state. HUD-approval and extension-count gates are restated for Summit extensions by the overwrite shared with task 0 (its replaced_by names both extension scopes); each sizing policy overwrites the extension-length clause with tails naming each other. Round 2 (T1-T1): the inherited base clause 'when the appraisal is older than appraisal_valid_months, a new appraisal is ordered, per reappraisal_for_extension' is overwritten for Summit extensions (both scopes named): the appraisal is not reordered at the grant; it is replaced by a new one when a payoff or sale is next evaluated. So with a 7-month appraisal on this world the grant is the only write and no handoff is owed; F2's reappraisal allowance is the time that later reappraisal needs.

5. FACTOR CARDS. Ask = 81 (baseline 90): sale_span (method, payoff) payoff terms issued, good-through 2026-11-20 -> 38 from 2026-10-13 | baseline 90 -> 90; payoff_funds_allowance (parameter, multi-source, payoff) net 973,450.00 covers required 642,118.40 -> +7 | 74; occupant_vacate_allowance (parameter, residency) latest finding 2026-08-10 occupied_by_others (near-miss: 2026-01-09 vacant is older) -> +10 | 71; appraisal_currency_allowance (parameter) 2026-02-10 is 7 months -> +14 | 67; filing_lead_allowance (parameter) request being replaced received 6 days before the deadline -> +5 | 76; reserve_charge_allowance (parameter, multi-source, setaside) active 1,240.55 < 9,635.00 -> +7 | 74. Further extension = 76 (baseline 90): current_document_measure (method) re-filed request rests on a financing commitment AND the payoff case has terms issued, good-through 2026-11-20 -> to 2026-11-30 = 48 | 90; balance_to_value_days (parameter) 56.48 -> +7 | 69; prior_grant_cut (parameter, multi-source) extension 1 rested on a listing agreement AND was granted 2026-07-08, 93 days ago -> -14 | 90; closing_charge_days (parameter, setaside; round 4, replaces sale_price_review) Summit reserve active, 1,240.55 < 9,635.00 (a year's tax and hazard premium) -> +7 | 69; household_occupant_days (parameter, residency) -> +7 | 69; reappraisal_allowance (parameter) 7 months -> +21 | 55. result MN(90, MX(30, 76)) = 76 -> 2026-12-28. The grant (76) stays below the 81 asked: Cedarline's measure stops at the scheduled closing plus 10 funds days, and the payoff statement is used once (round 3 removed the separate readiness addition that counted the same closing interval again).

6. FACTOR INDEPENDENCE. Ask: sale_span<-payoff case/requests + deadline_now; payoff_funds<-contract + issued terms; occupant<-residency_events; appraisal<-appraisal_date; filing_lead<-pending request date + deadline_now; reserve<-setaside. Grant: measure<-request document/date + statement good-through date + deadline_now; equity<-jumbo balance + case_appraised_value (a plain binding stated once in the rule; no other grant factor divides by the appraisal); prior_grant<-latest grant date + latest accepted request document; closing_charge<-setaside reserve status, balance and annual charges; the payoff statement good-through date is read only inside current_document_measure (declared in its bindings); occupant<-residency_events; reappraisal<-appraisal_date. pending_requests is a plain guard in both results. No factor reads another factor's binding. Method pairs: sale_span statement vs contract (issued statement present vs not), statement vs plan (same), contract vs plan (accepted contract present vs not); current_document_measure commitment+statement vs commitment+60 (good-through date present vs not), commitment vs plan days (document type), commitment+statement vs plan (document type). Reachable-domain table: see task 0 section 17 (all tiers of both policies reachable within scope; the universal 'awaiting a decision' and 'already granted' parts removed).

7. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Both writes: maturity_extensions extension_request_on_file (step 12: pending request rq_extB received, listing agreement; step 14: the re-filed request from step 12) and extension_before_deadline (time, anchor resolution_deadline 2026-10-13, not_after, inclusive: 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-09 receipts qualify; a 2026-10-14 receipt would be declined). HUD/count gates restated: Summit approved by Cedarline, number 2 = one granted + 1, max 2 for the Principal Residence Change plan. Reappraisal clause restated (no order at the grant for Summit extensions).

8. BUSINESS OBJECT / ROWS. Case 956e... (single open case, extension_period). Requests: rq_intent (sell, accepted), rq_extA (accepted, behind extension 1: listing agreement -> prior-grant cut), rq_extB (received, stale listing: the state the grant waits on and the filing-lead anchor). Events: two call-day notices, extension 1 and its letter (granted count = 1). Payoff case (terms issued, good-through 2026-11-20, required 642,118.40) and its contract (net covers payoff). Residency inspections: vacant (older decoy) and occupied_by_others (latest). Reserve active, low. Summit balance. Each removal changes a tier as listed in the factor cards.

9. PROBLEM TREE. Edge further_extension_sizing <- further_extension_ask, value_input on measured_extension, state form: "A further extension is not granted until the case carries an extension request awaiting a decision whose supporting document is dated no more than 30 days before the day that request was received." False at opening: rq_extB evidence_date 2026-03-01 vs request_date 2026-10-07. Only the re-filing tool files extension requests, so the state names a unique write. Skip run: without the re-filing the request awaiting a decision is the stale listing request, measured as the plan's 90: 90 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 21 - 14 = 118, capped 90 (vs 76).

10. PERSONA. Precise, formal 81-year-old; volunteers the move, sale under contract, payoff statement good through November 20, the October 13 deadline and her October 7 mailed request; gives the lender commitment (FNB-MC-2026-55841, 2026-10-05) only when asked for newer paperwork; never mentions re-filing; stops on hearing the new deadline. No extra asks.

11. STANDARD SOLUTION (15 actions): find_customers(name) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> find_maturity_cases -> find_maturity_requests -> find_maturity_case_events -> find_jumbo_loans -> find_payoff_cases -> find_payoff_requests -> find_residency_profiles -> find_residency_events -> find_setaside_accounts -> unlock_user/call_user re-filing (rq_extB, financing_commitment, FNB-MC-2026-55841, 2026-10-05, 81) -> unlock/call grant (mrq_f5316e17b77e from the receipt, Dolores, number 2, 76) -> deadline 2026-12-28. No reappraisal order and no handoff.

12. VERIFICATION (round 2 full block). EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK; traceability misses only unlock tool names. Probes: round 1 (lapsed payoff case, declined cheaper contract, declined later commitment request, inspection order without outcome) and round 2 (an older extension letter dated 2026-03-01 among case events, a withdrawn payoff case with a later good-through date) — results unchanged 81/76 (round 3 adds a declined lower-priced contract, excluded by 'accepted'). Absent cases: no payoff case -> span contract+45 or plan days, measure commitment+60, no payoff additions; no inspection -> 0; no appraisal -> missing tiers; no reserve -> 0; no prior grant on record -> nothing taken off (round 5); no request awaiting a decision -> guards give 0. Extensions floored at 30 days.

13. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. The rules, the lookups and her answers give the same two writes and figures; the selection points (which payoff case: terms issued; which contract: accepted; which request: most recently received awaiting a decision; which finding: latest) are stated in the rules.

14. REVISION LOG (round 2). T1-T1: Summit-extension overwrite of the reappraisal-at-grant clause (no tool exists to order one; the base appraisal rule orders it at the next payoff/sale evaluation) — one correct action sequence. CG-3e: measure tiers rebuilt (commitment with payoff statement / commitment / listing) -> 83 -> 79; CG-3f: prior_grant_cut keyed to the prior grant's document and age; filing lead tiers lose the universal 'awaiting a decision' part (guard stated separately); zero-day extensions replaced by a 30-day floor. Proof text (traces, closure, tracing, rationale) swept for 83 / 2027-01-04.

15. REVISION LOG (round 3, audit r2). R2-N2: the further-extension prerequisite's effect now states both measure paths (good-through + 10 with issued payoff terms, otherwise commitment + 60) instead of only commitment + 60. O2-2 (double count): payoff_readiness removed; replaced by sale_price_review (contract price against the as-is appraisal: below 95 / 95 to 100 / 100 or more), a distinct review Cedarline performs; the good-through date is now bound inside the measure factor. Gold 79 -> 76 (deadline 2026-12-28); traces, closure, tracing and dossier swept. Overwrite replaced_by sentences reordered (in-force base content first, own scope second); probes re-run: 81/76 unchanged under decoys, skip A gives 90.

16. REVISION LOG (round 4, audit r3). R3-N1: sale_price_review removed — a below-appraisal price review has no weight on a sale whose net proceeds (973,450.00) repay the 642,118.40 payoff in full (non-recourse: the 95 percent test matters only for a short sale, which the ask's payoff_funds_allowance already covers). Replaced by closing_charge_days (cross-difficulty setaside): the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve active but below one year's property tax and hazard premium -> +7 for clearing the coming charges at closing, depleted -> +14, otherwise 0 — the same premise and tiers as the ask's reserve_charge_allowance, so the grant honours the reserve time the re-filing asks for. Her reserve: active, 1,240.55 < 9,635.00 -> +7; gold stays 76 (2026-12-28), baseline 90; factor_sensitivity 69. Payoff read on the grant side is now only the statement good-through date (measure). O3-3: case_appraised_value is a plain binding stated once in the rule and used only by the equity share. O3-1 (charter): first-extension deadline_now basis now quotes the rule verbatim. Probes: reserve at exactly 9,635.00 -> 69, at 9,634.99 -> 76, depleted -> 83, closed or absent -> 69, depleted decoy on another loan or a HECM LESA -> 69 (loan- and variant-scoped), appraised value missing or zero -> equity 100 -> 69. Traces, tracing, necessity lines and dossier swept.

17. REVISION LOG (round 5, render_source r1 + XF recipe). Figures unchanged: A 81, F2 76 (2026-12-28), baselines 90/90, factor sensitivities unchanged. A3: the ask's baseline defines the span (plan days as standard) and the requested length (span with every addition), limited to the plan days after every addition; each addition is 'added to the requested length'. A2: F2's baseline defines the measured extension (plan days as standard) and the extension length (measured extension with every addition and deduction), raised to 30 then limited to the plan days after every addition and deduction; each factor names the extension length. B: the reappraisal replaced_by restates the plan's reappraisal-for-extension setting and no longer defers to a base rule. C13: the unused document_current gate and its request_received/current_evidence_days inputs are removed (the 30-day currency test is the prerequisite sentence, a state gate); with no granted extension on record nothing is taken off (no 0-day default); a document of another kind or an undated one -> evidence insufficient, zero days. C14: a span ending before the current deadline is zero; a missing commission or other cost counts as zero; the filing lead has no 999 sentinel; appraisal ages have no -1 sentinel (dated after the event -> under 4 months). Probes: skip A (stale listing request) -> F2 measured 90, result 90; good-through before the deadline -> span 0; commission missing -> net = price less other costs; no prior grant -> cut 0.

18. REVISION LOG (round 6, audit policy_task r5, R5-N1). Same-day ties now carry stated tie rules implemented by a two-step pick (latest date, then latest recorded time on that date): F2 and A — extension requests received on one day: the one recorded later, so a request re-filed on the day of the request it replaces is the one a grant rests on; F2 — accepted requests received on one day: the one recorded later; A — accepted purchase contracts received on one day: the one recorded later; A and F2 — inspection findings on one date: occupied by someone other than a borrower over vacant over any other finding. The re-filing tool now stamps created_at as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, the records' own form. No tie in this world; figures unchanged (81/76). Probes: a same-day stale listing recorded before the re-filing -> 76, recorded after it -> 90; the original request moved to the re-filing day and recorded earlier -> 76; a same-day accepted commitment recorded after the 06-26 listing -> no cut, 90 (recorded before -> 76); a same-day short contract recorded later -> shortfall tier, 90 (earlier -> 81); latest finding vacant plus a same-day occupied finding -> occupied tier (76/81).
user_scenario:
You are Dolores Nakamura, 81, a retired school librarian who now lives at Brightwater Senior Living in Cary. You are polite, precise and a little formal, you like to have things repeated back to you, and you call Cedarline yourself because you prefer to handle your own affairs. You open by explaining that you moved out of your house at 3107 Churchill Road in Raleigh last year, that your Cedarline Summit loan on it was called due, and that you are selling the house: you have a buyer under contract, the title company has a payoff statement from Cedarline good through November 20, and closing is set for that date. Your letters say the house has to be resolved by October 13, and you mailed Cedarline a request for more time on October 7. You want Cedarline to move the deadline so the sale can close in November; you are happy for the agent to do whatever Cedarline does on its side, and you will do yourself anything that must come from you.

To be found, give your full name, Dolores Nakamura. To verify, give your phone number 4155548143 and your date of birth, 1944-11-02 (November 2, 1944); give your email, dolores.nakamura@yahoo.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 4096, only if asked for more. Your loan number, 7436120947, you give only when asked. If the agent asks what you sent with the October 7 request, say you enclosed the same listing agreement you sent in June, signed in March. If the agent asks whether you have any newer paperwork about the sale, say you have a commitment letter from the buyer's lender, number FNB-MC-2026-55841, dated 2026-10-05 (October 5, 2026), and read the number out exactly as printed. If asked who is at the house, say your grandson has been staying there since the summer to look after it and will be out before closing. If asked about the contract, say the price is 1,035,000 dollars and the title company has all the figures.

You do not know Cedarline's procedures and you never suggest any. If the agent explains that something has to come from you and hands it to you to complete, you do it at once with exactly the reference numbers, document details and figure the agent gives you, and you read back what your confirmation shows; you never make up figures yourself.

When the agent tells you the deadline has been moved and gives you the new date, you repeat it back, thank the agent and end the call. If the agent tells you the deadline cannot be moved today, you ask once what happens next, accept the answer and end the call.

edges.condition: The most recently received maturity_requests row of type extension_request with request_status received carries an evidence_date no more than 30 days before its request_date.
edges.policy_source: A further extension is not granted until the case carries an extension request awaiting a decision whose supporting document is dated no more than 30 days before the day that request was received.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only extension request awaiting a decision (received 2026-10-07) rests on the listing agreement dated 2026-03-01, 220 days before it was received, so the case carries no request with current supporting evidence.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Dolores's re-filing files a newer request received 2026-10-09 resting on the financing commitment dated 2026-10-05 (4 days earlier), so the measured extension runs to 10 days after the payoff statement's good-through date (48) and the further extension is 76 instead of 90.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge: the further extension waits on a request with current evidence, which only the customer's re-filing creates; the re-filing comes first and the grant second. No parallel writes.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the re-filing the request awaiting a decision still rests on the stale listing agreement, the measured extension is the plan's 90 days: 90 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 21 - 14 = 118, capped at 90, so extension_days 90 instead of 76 (and the grant would rest on a request whose evidence is not current); the terminal state also lacks the re-filed request.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: Dolores only asks for the October 13 deadline to be moved so the November 20 closing can happen and mentions she mailed a request on October 7; she never says her paperwork is out of date or that anything must be re-filed. The buyer's commitment letter details are given only when the agent asks for newer paperwork, and she runs the re-filing only when the agent hands it to her.
